title:
讓・傅凱
掌中的宏偉世界

Jean Fouquet
A world in miniature
body: 十五世紀法國的面孔、信仰與王權
Faces, faith and royal power in fifteenth-century France
caption:
艾蒂安・舍瓦利耶時禱書：聖母領報
1450 年代，羊皮紙彩飾，孔代博物館

Hours of Étienne Chevalier: The Annunciation
1450s, illuminated parchment, Musée Condé
tw: 這幅畫原本小到可以捧在手中，裡面的建築和人物卻像一座完整世界。十五世紀的法國畫家讓・傅凱，如何讓一張臉、一部祈禱書，甚至一場古代戰爭，都具有這樣的存在感？今天，我們就從他的十二件作品線索，走進這個精巧而宏偉的世界。
en: This image once belonged to a book you could hold in your hands. Yet its architecture feels spacious, and its figures seem to have real weight. How did the French painter Jean Fouquet give a face, a prayer book, and even an ancient battle such presence? Twelve works offer a way into his world.

title: 一幅失傳的教宗肖像
A lost portrait in Rome
body:
教宗恩仁四世肖像
約 1444–1446 年，原作失傳

Portrait of Pope Eugene IV
About 1444–1446. Original lost
detail: 文獻留下聲望，沒有留下可供重建的原畫
Written testimony preserves its reputation, but cannot restore its appearance
caption:
讓・傅凱的義大利活動
原作媒材見文獻記載，無現存作品可核驗

Fouquet’s activity in Italy
No surviving original allows direct technical examination
tw: 認識傅凱，可以從一件看不見的作品開始。約一四四四至一四四六年，他在義大利的活動與教宗恩仁四世肖像相連。文字證言保存了他的聲望，原畫卻已失傳，因此這裡刻意不放一張替代肖像。羅馬經驗讓我們理解，他後來的藝術來自跨地域的交流：人物的體積、建築的深度，可以和北方細緻的觀察相互結合。不過，旅行的每一步和確切學習對象仍有空白。我們能沿著現存作品看見這些方法如何發揮作用，卻不能替失去的畫補上顏色與表情。
en: Our story begins with an image we can no longer see. Around fourteen forty-four to fourteen forty-six, Fouquet’s activity in Italy included a portrait of Pope Eugene the Fourth. Written testimony preserves its reputation, but the original is lost. We therefore leave its appearance open. His Italian experience provides a useful context for the solid figures and architectural spaces in later works. These meet a northern interest in precise faces and surfaces. Still, the surviving evidence does not give us a complete travel diary or a proven list of teachers. The missing portrait reminds us to distinguish what documents establish from what surviving paintings allow us to observe.

title: 沒有王冠的國王
A king without a crown
body:
寬闊紅袍建立威嚴
具體面孔保留個性

A broad red silhouette conveys authority
A particular face preserves individuality
caption:
查理七世肖像，約 1445–1450 年
讓・傅凱，橡木板油彩，羅浮宮 INV 9106

Portrait of Charles VII, about 1445–1450
Jean Fouquet, oil on oak, Louvre INV 9106
tw: 查理七世沒有戴王冠，也沒有舉起武器，卻幾乎填滿畫面。先退一步看，帽子、肩膀與紅袍形成穩固輪廓，兩側帷幕把我們的目光留在人物身上。再靠近一些，鼻子、眼睛和嘴唇又顯出無法由任何人代替的個性。傅凱把君王的職位交給一具具體身體承擔。羅浮宮將畫作定在約一四四五至一四五〇年，其他研究也有較晚定年，因此不能把它說成某次勝戰的確切紀念。更有意思的是，十九世紀入冊時，作品曾被歸給不知名的希臘畫家。今天看來熟悉的作者身分，其實經過後人的辨認才逐步穩定。畫面保存了國王的面孔，收藏史則讓傅凱的名字重新浮現。
en: Charles the Seventh wears no crown and raises no weapon. His presence comes first from the broad shape of his body. Step back, and the hat, shoulders, and red robe form a stable silhouette. The curtains keep our attention close to him. Move nearer, and the eyes, nose, and lips become distinctly individual. Fouquet allows a recognizable person to carry the authority of kingship. The Louvre dates the portrait to about fourteen forty-five to fourteen fifty, while other studies place it later. We should therefore avoid tying it to one particular victory. Its later history brings another surprise. A nineteenth-century inventory attributed it to an unknown Greek painter. The king’s face survived, but identifying Fouquet’s hand required later scholarship. The painting preserves one identity while its collection history reveals the recovery of another.

title: 大臣的祈禱有重量
The weight of a prayer
body:
紅袍與金色建築呈現地位
合掌把視線引向畫外

Red cloth and golden architecture signal status
Joined hands direct attention beyond the frame
caption:
紀堯姆・朱韋內爾・德・于爾桑肖像，約 1450–1460 年
讓・傅凱，橡木板油彩，羅浮宮 INV 9619

Guillaume Jouvenel des Ursins, about 1450–1460
Jean Fouquet, oil on oak, Louvre INV 9619
tw: 這位身穿紅袍的大臣，同樣有寬厚的身體，觀看方向卻和國王不同。他的雙手合攏，朝向畫外的神聖對象。紅袍讓他穩穩留在畫內，祈禱又把關係延伸出去。背景的金色建築與繁複裝飾，也讓我們看見他的尊榮。朱韋內爾曾擔任法國掌璽大臣，這份現世地位與宗教姿態可以存在於同一幅肖像中。請留意雙手如何把衣袍的大面積，收束成一個安靜而集中的動作。至於畫外原本是否另有一塊配對畫板，現有資料仍不足以讓我們重建。這件畫在十九世紀還曾被歸給杜勒，後來又改歸沃爾格穆特。重新辨認傅凱，也意味著學者逐漸看懂這種法國肖像特有的安排。
en: This powerful man also wears a broad red robe, but his gesture changes the encounter. Guillaume Jouvenel des Ursins joins his hands in prayer toward a sacred presence beyond the picture. His body anchors our attention inside the frame, while his hands carry it outward. Golden architecture and intricate decoration make his social position visible. He served as chancellor of France, and the painting gives that office considerable weight. Religious devotion and worldly distinction occupy the same space. Notice how the small, concentrated movement of the fingers gathers the much larger mass of the robe. We cannot confidently reconstruct a missing companion panel from that gesture alone. The portrait’s later attributions also shifted, first to Dürer and then to Wolgemut. Recognizing Fouquet meant learning to see how these particular choices belonged together.

title: 兩翼之間的祈禱
Prayer across two panels
body: 左翼的凡人朝向右翼的聖母子
A donor on the left turns toward the Virgin and Child on the right
caption:
默倫雙聯畫，約 1452–1455 年，木板油彩
讓・傅凱；左翼柏林繪畫館，右翼安特衛普皇家美術館

Melun Diptych, about 1452–1455, oil on panel
Jean Fouquet. Left: Gemäldegalerie, Berlin. Right: KMSKA, Antwerp
tw: 把默倫雙聯畫的兩翼一起看，祈禱才有了完整方向。左邊的舍瓦利耶合掌跪禱，聖斯德望在身旁引介他。聖人手上的書與石塊，指向遭石擊殉道的身分。右邊則是蒼白的聖母子，以及密集的紅藍天使。左翼的建築讓人覺得可以走入，右翼卻像一個超越日常的神聖世界。清楚輪廓和圓整體積，又讓兩邊保持呼應。這件作品原來與默倫教堂的紀念空間相連，畫框還有絨布、珠飾與圓章。約一七七三年拆散後，兩翼走進不同收藏，今天分藏柏林與安特衛普。這張並置照片讓我們重新讀到跨越兩翼的關係，但原有畫框的工藝和教堂中的觀看環境，已無法只靠影像拼接恢復。
en: The Melun Diptych becomes easier to understand when we see both wings together. On the left, Étienne Chevalier prays beside Saint Stephen. The saint’s book and stones refer to his martyrdom by stoning. On the right, the pale Virgin and Child appear among brilliant red and blue angels. The donor’s architectural setting feels accessible, while the sacred vision seems removed from everyday life. Clear contours and rounded forms connect the two worlds. The work belonged to a commemorative setting in Melun, and its original frame included velvet, pearls, and medallions. Around seventeen seventy-three, the ensemble was dismantled. The panels eventually entered collections in Berlin and Antwerp. Placing their images together helps us follow the direction of prayer again. It cannot fully recover the precious frame or the original experience of seeing the work in its church.

title: 紅與藍托起白色肌膚
White skin among red and blue
body:
色差先吸引目光
安靜姿態延長凝視

Strong color contrasts attract the eye
Stillness holds it there
caption:
默倫雙聯畫右翼：天使環繞的聖母子
讓・傅凱，約 1450–1455 年，木板油彩，KMSKA 132

Melun Diptych, right wing: Virgin and Child with Angels
Jean Fouquet, about 1450–1455, oil on panel, KMSKA 132
tw: 現在靠近右翼，看看傅凱如何讓一個近在眼前的身體，仍然保有神聖的距離。第一個吸引目光的是白色：聖母與幼兒的肌膚被紅藍天使包圍，幾乎像雕塑般突出。接著，眼睛沿著冠冕、珍珠與寶座移動，才發現華麗表面藏著細小反光。人物輪廓很清楚，臉上的表情卻相當克制。強烈色差抓住注意，平靜姿態則讓觀看停留。聖母裸露乳房，與哺乳聖母的宗教傳統相連，也和天上王后的冠冕同時存在。球形身體、幼兒與天使的頭部，讓全幅形成反覆呼應的曲線。至於她是否採用了阿涅絲・索蕾的容貌，館方也保留不同意見。這個問題很吸引人，卻不必取代畫面本身：傅凱讓母性、宮廷美貌與神聖權威，集中在一個極其安定的形象裡。我們可以討論這種安排的效果，無須把模特兒身分說成已經證實的宮廷祕聞。
en: Look closely at the right wing and notice how a body placed so near us can still feel distant. White is the first attraction. The pale skin of the Virgin and Child stands out against the red and blue angels with an almost sculptural clarity. Our eyes then travel through the crown, pearls, and throne, where tiny reflections reward closer attention. Sharp contours make every form legible, while the restrained faces slow the emotional pace. Strong color catches us, and stillness keeps us looking. The exposed breast belongs to the religious tradition of the nursing Virgin. Here it shares the same figure with a heavenly queen’s crown. Rounded bodies and angel heads create related curves across the surface. Whether the Virgin resembles Agnès Sorel remains a matter of debate, including in the museum’s own discussion. That possibility need not dominate everything we see. Fouquet brings maternal care, courtly beauty, and sacred authority into one exceptionally controlled image. Its effect remains compelling even when the model’s identity stays uncertain.

title: 畫家把自己留在框邊
The painter at the edge
body:
面孔與姓名同時出現
直徑僅約 7.2 公分

A face accompanies a name
Only about 7.2 centimeters across
caption:
圓章自畫像，約 1452–1455 年
讓・傅凱，銅胎彩繪琺瑯與金色單色畫，羅浮宮 OA 56

Self-Portrait Medallion, about 1452–1455
Jean Fouquet, painted enamel and gold on copper, Louvre OA 56
tw: 這張臉在螢幕上很醒目，原物的直徑卻只有約七點二公分。金色線面從深底浮現，周圍的名字讓製作者可以被辨認。這枚銅胎琺瑯圓章原來屬於默倫雙聯畫的畫框。想像一下觀看順序：先是聖母子與祈禱者，再是框邊一個小小的畫家身影。他讓自己可見，也保留整件宗教作品的主次。今天圓章獨立收藏於羅浮宮，很容易讓人把它看成單獨的自我宣言。放回原來關係，它同時具有裝飾、署名與紀念的作用。我們不必宣布它是歐洲第一幅自畫像，才能理解它的重要。在為別人製作的奉獻物裡，傅凱把自己的名字和面孔一起留下。細小尺度反而讓這個選擇更值得注意。
en: This face looks commanding on a screen, but the original measures only about seven point two centimeters across. Gold lines and shading emerge from a dark surface, while the surrounding name identifies the maker. The enamel medallion originally belonged to the frame of the Melun Diptych. Imagine the order of attention. First came the Virgin, Child, donor, and saint. Only then might a viewer discover the painter at the edge. Fouquet made himself visible within the hierarchy of a religious commission. Now preserved separately in the Louvre, the object can seem like an independent declaration of artistic identity. Its original setting also gave it the functions of ornament, signature, and remembrance. We do not need to call it Europe’s first self-portrait to appreciate the choice. A maker placed both his name and his face inside an object created for someone else.

title: 書頁容得下一片天地
A landscape inside a book
body:
近景人物帶入故事
遠方建築擴大空間

Figures bring the story close
Distant buildings extend the world
caption:
艾蒂安・舍瓦利耶時禱書：聖瑪加利大與奧利布里烏斯
讓・傅凱，約 1452–1460 年，羊皮紙彩飾，羅浮宮 M.I. 1093

Hours of Étienne Chevalier: Saint Margaret and Olibrius
Jean Fouquet, about 1452–1460, illuminated parchment, Louvre M.I. 1093
tw: 從祭壇畫轉向時禱書，觀看的身體動作也改變了。舍瓦利耶的祈禱書原本可以在近處翻閱，圖像伴隨日常時段的禱文。這頁聖瑪加利大與奧利布里烏斯，把人物、動物和遠方建築放進同一片風景。近處的動作讓我們進入故事，背景則提示一個還在延伸的世界。如此小的表面，仍能讓人分辨身體重量、前後距離和不同活動。請注意，宏偉感來自關係的清楚，不必依賴巨大尺寸。書中的姓名縮寫，又讓委託人的身分反覆進入祈禱。這樣的物件既能表達財力，也能真誠用於宗教生活。傅凱的工作，是讓私人身分和神聖敘事在翻頁之間持續相遇。今日把圖像放大，我們更容易看清細節，也需要記住它原來貼近雙手的尺度。
en: Moving from an altarpiece to a book of hours changes the viewer’s physical relationship with an image. Chevalier’s book brought pictures close to the hands and linked them with prayers organized through the day. In this scene of Saint Margaret and Olibrius, figures, animals, and distant buildings inhabit one landscape. Nearby actions draw us into the event, while the background suggests a world continuing beyond it. On a small surface, Fouquet makes bodily weight and spatial distance legible. Monumentality comes from clear relationships rather than physical size. Repeated initials elsewhere in the book also bring the patron’s identity into prayer. Such an object could display wealth and serve sincere devotion. Its functions could coexist. Enlarging the page helps us notice details today, but remembering its original scale restores something of the intimacy that shaped its design.
extraSource: Specific image identification and current collection: https://classes.bnf.fr/fouquet/grand/f122.htm. Photo credit: RMN, as credited by BnF.

title: 從翻頁的書到牆上的畫
A book becomes framed pictures
body:
十八世紀拆散
1891 年，四十張彩飾在尚蒂伊重聚

Dismantled in the eighteenth century
Forty miniatures reunited at Chantilly in 1891
caption:
艾蒂安・舍瓦利耶時禱書：基督受難
讓・傅凱，1450 年代，羊皮紙彩飾，孔代博物館

Hours of Étienne Chevalier: The Crucifixion
Jean Fouquet, 1450s, illuminated parchment, Musée Condé
tw: 看這頁基督受難時，試著想像它的前後還有禱文和其他圖像。原本的閱讀會隨翻頁推進，也會反覆回到熟悉的故事。十八世紀，舍瓦利耶時禱書遭到拆散。從此，一件供人使用的書，逐漸變成可以個別收藏的小畫。一八九一年，奧馬爾公爵取得其中四十張彩飾，在尚蒂伊形成今天的重要核心。這次重聚讓圖像重新被共同觀看，卻沒有恢復原書的裝訂和全部閱讀順序。其他散頁仍然分藏各處。收藏因此同時帶來保存與改變：畫面獲得獨立展示的機會，原先的文字關係卻變得不容易察覺。當我們欣賞清楚的人群與空間，也可以多問一句，這張畫原本伴隨什麼閱讀行為？這個問題能把名畫重新帶回一本書的生命。
en: As you look at the Crucifixion, imagine prayers and other images before and after this page. Reading once moved through that sequence and returned to familiar scenes. The Hours of Étienne Chevalier was dismantled in the eighteenth century. A book made for use gradually became a group of pictures that could circulate separately. In eighteen ninety-one, the Duke of Aumale acquired forty miniatures, creating the major surviving group at Chantilly. Their reunion allowed viewers to see them together, but it did not restore the original binding or the complete reading order. Other leaves remain elsewhere. Collecting brought preservation and transformation at the same time. An individual image gained prominence while its connections with text became harder to see. Alongside admiring Fouquet’s figures and spaces, we can ask what acts of reading this picture originally accompanied.

title: 祈禱書也有自己的入口
A personal entrance to prayer
body:
傅凱製作六幅卷首彩飾
全書由多位畫家合作

Fouquet supplied six opening miniatures
Several illuminators worked on the book
caption:
西蒙・德・瓦里時禱書：聖母子，1455 年
讓・傅凱，羊皮紙彩飾，海牙 KB，74 G 37a

Hours of Simon de Varie: Virgin and Child, 1455
Jean Fouquet, illuminated parchment, KB, The Hague, 74 G 37a
tw: 瓦里的時禱書提醒我們，一位畫家不必完成每一頁，也能決定整部書的第一印象。傅凱為一四五五年的這部書製作六幅卷首彩飾，其他部分則由不同畫家參與。這幅聖母子的面孔、披巾與裝飾邊界，把閱讀開始的時刻變成一場安靜相遇。原書的捐獻者肖像和紋章，又使祈禱與某個具體的人相連。瓦里來自王室財政網絡，圖像中的身分呈現不能直接當作職業履歷。尤其盔甲形象，並不足以證明他曾參加戰役。後來原書分成三冊，今天分藏洛杉磯與海牙。跨館比對讓學者重新理解人物和紋章之間的關係。對我們而言，這件作品的精彩，也在於它把一組經過安排的開場，變成使用者進入整部祈禱書的方式。
en: Simon de Varie’s book shows how a painter could shape an entire reading experience without painting every page. Fouquet supplied six opening miniatures for the manuscript dated fourteen fifty-five. Other illuminators contributed to the rest. Here, the Virgin and Child, their drapery, and the decorated boundary make the beginning of reading feel like a quiet encounter. The patron’s portrait and heraldry elsewhere connect prayer with a particular person. Varie belonged to the royal financial world, and his chosen appearance should not be mistaken for a straightforward professional record. Armor in a portrait cannot prove participation in battle. The book later became three volumes, now divided between Los Angeles and The Hague. Comparing the dispersed material helped scholars reconnect images and identity. Fouquet’s contribution demonstrates the power of a carefully designed entrance into a larger book.

title: 聖路加的工作空間
Inside Saint Luke’s workspace
body:
執筆、繪像與醫療器物
細節讓聖人的角色可被辨識

Writing, painting and medical vessels
Objects make the saint’s roles visible
caption:
讓・羅貝爾泰時禱書，聖路加，第 15 葉正面
讓・傅凱，約 1460 年代，羊皮紙彩飾，摩根圖書館 MS M.834

Hours of Jean Robertet, Saint Luke, fol. 15r
Jean Fouquet, about the 1460s, illuminated vellum, Morgan MS M.834
tw: 這頁聖路加像帶我們走進一間工作室。他在書前執筆，身旁的牛提示福音作者身分，後方的聖母畫又呼應他為聖母繪像的傳統。架上的玻璃器物，則與醫師的工作相連。傅凱讓細節各有位置，也各有辨識作用。請看看人物如何成為中心，而地板與牆面又把小房間向後展開。這並非古代聖人的工作室實錄，而是以十五世紀熟悉的器物，讓宗教角色變得可理解。整部羅貝爾泰時禱書也有時間層次：摩根將最初九幅全頁畫歸於傅凱，其他十六幅歸於科隆布。今天的書名，並不表示傅凱一開始就直接為羅貝爾泰完成全書。不同縮寫、續作和後來裝訂，共同留下它逐步形成的痕跡。書頁的精緻，因而也保存了一段合作與接續的歷史。
en: Saint Luke seems to welcome us into a working room. He writes at a book, while the ox identifies him as an evangelist. A painting of the Virgin recalls the tradition that he painted her portrait. Glass vessels evoke his medical role. Fouquet gives these objects clear places and recognizable purposes. Notice how the figure holds the composition together while the floor and walls carry the room backward. This is a fifteenth-century visual explanation of a saint, rather than a literal record of an ancient workshop. The manuscript itself also contains layers of time. The Morgan attributes the first nine full-page miniatures to Fouquet and sixteen others to Jean Colombe. Its present name does not establish that Fouquet originally made the whole book for Robertet. Initials, later work, and rebinding preserve evidence of changing ownership and continued production.

title: 席位讓王權一目了然
Power arranged around a table
body:
查理五世的 1378 年宴會
透過十五世紀的眼光重新呈現

Charles V’s banquet of 1378
Reimagined through fifteenth-century eyes
caption:
法蘭西大編年史：查理五世宴會，約 1455–1460 年
讓・傅凱，羊皮紙彩飾，法國國家圖書館 Français 6465

Grandes Chroniques de France: Banquet of Charles V, about 1455–1460
Jean Fouquet, illuminated parchment, BnF Français 6465
tw: 宴會裡最先被看懂的，往往是誰坐在哪裡。這頁描繪查理五世在一三七八年接待皇帝的場面，傅凱卻透過十五世紀的服飾和空間來重新構想。遠端的主桌安定，前景侍從忙碌，白色桌布和藍色王室紋樣引導目光。地磚幫助我們向後觀看，卻不必每一條線都匯到同一個消失點。這種安排優先讓禮儀關係清楚可讀。原來龐大的人群和漫長活動，被選成一幅容易記住的歷史場景。全書的加冕、會面與行軍，也以類似方式讓王朝持續可見。至於原書是否為查理七世製作，館方仍保留可能的語氣。理解它如何塑造王權，不需要先替委託人做出確定答案。位置、尺度與觀看方向，已經把政治秩序轉成眼睛能讀懂的形式。
en: At a banquet, seating can reveal power before anyone speaks. This miniature represents Charles the Fifth receiving the emperor in thirteen seventy-eight, but Fouquet reimagines the occasion through fifteenth-century clothing and surroundings. The distant main table remains stable while attendants animate the foreground. White cloth and royal blue guide the eye. Floor tiles suggest recession without requiring every line to meet at one mathematically consistent point. The arrangement makes ceremonial relationships readable. A much larger gathering and a longer event become one memorable historical scene. Coronations, meetings, and campaigns elsewhere in the chronicle similarly give the dynasty a visible life. Charles the Seventh remains a possible original recipient rather than a proven patron. We can understand how the image organizes royal authority without settling that question. Position, scale, and direction already make political order visible.

title: 一個新制度的集體形象
A new order takes visible form
body:
相同禮服表現歸屬
中央座位表現階序

Shared robes establish membership
The central throne establishes rank
caption:
路易十一主持聖米歇爾騎士團會議，約 1469–1470 年
讓・傅凱，羊皮紙彩飾，法國國家圖書館 Français 19819，fol. 1r

Louis XI and the Order of Saint Michael, about 1469–1470
Jean Fouquet, illuminated parchment, BnF Français 19819, fol. 1r
tw: 在這間小廳裡，國王坐在中央，騎士沿兩側排列，前景的空地把我們與王座隔開。相近的白色禮服表現共同身分，位置高低則維持等級。牆上的聖米歇爾圖像，又把團體的宗教主保放在國王上方。這是騎士團章程的卷首畫，並非某次會議的現場快照。路易十一在一四六九年創立騎士團，章程甚至要求在書的開頭畫出君主與最初的騎士。因此圖像是新制度的一部分，讓成員反覆看見自己應當如何圍繞君王。個別面孔看起來不同，卻不代表我們已能替每個人確定姓名。傅凱運用緊湊的室內空間，把團結與尊卑同時安排得清楚。讀者還沒讀到規則，就先看見了這個團體希望維持的共同樣貌。
en: The king occupies the center, with knights arranged along both sides of a small room. Open floor separates us from the throne. Similar white robes establish a shared identity, while placement preserves differences in rank. Saint Michael’s image above the king identifies the order’s heavenly patron. This is the opening miniature of a rule book, rather than a snapshot of a particular meeting. Louis the Eleventh founded the order in fourteen sixty-nine, and its statutes explicitly required an opening image of the sovereign and the first knights. The picture therefore helped give a new institution visible form. Different faces suggest individual members, but they do not supply a securely identified attendance list. Fouquet’s compact interior makes collective belonging and hierarchy readable together. Before readers reach the rules, they encounter the organized body those rules were intended to sustain.

title: 戰爭有近景，也有遠方
The battle and the distant world
body:
前景的身體衝突
後方的軍勢與平靜地景

Bodies collide in the foreground
Armies and quiet landscape unfold beyond
caption:
羅馬人與迦太基人之戰，通稱坎尼會戰，約 1470–1475 年
讓・傅凱；邊飾另有作者，羊皮紙彩飾，羅浮宮 RF 5271

Battle between Romans and Carthaginians, known as Cannae, about 1470–1475
Jean Fouquet. Border by another artist. Illuminated parchment, Louvre RF 5271
tw: 先看前排交戰的身體：舉起的劍、跨開的腿，以及倒下的人。往後移動視線，個別人物逐漸變成密集軍隊，再往上則是水面、遠山和天空。傅凱讓一場戰爭同時具有可以近看的動作與難以數盡的規模。金色提亮把前排盔甲從群體中帶出，也呼應書頁的華麗邊飾。不過，羅浮宮把邊飾歸給另一位畫家，不能全算作傅凱的筆跡。這張散頁原屬古代史手抄本，下方文字是理解畫面的重要部分。館方題名保留通稱坎尼會戰的限定，所以我們也不能把每一支隊伍，直接對照到古代戰役的戰術位置。遠方的平靜與近處的暴力形成張力，可以引發對戰爭的思考，卻還不足以證明畫家留下了反戰宣言。一張小書頁，讓我們在個別生命與巨大事件之間往返觀看。
en: Begin with the bodies at the front. A sword waits to fall, legs brace for combat, and fallen figures interrupt the action. Farther back, individuals merge into a dense army. Beyond them lie water, hills, and sky. Fouquet makes war readable at the scale of a body and at the scale of a crowd. Gold highlights separate the nearest armor and echo the decorated page. The Louvre attributes that border to another artist, so its details should not all become evidence of Fouquet’s hand. The leaf came from an ancient-history manuscript, and the text below belongs to its meaning. The museum retains the qualification “known as Cannae.” We should likewise avoid mapping each group onto a securely reconstructed ancient battle plan. Quiet distance and nearby violence create tension. They invite reflection without proving a documented antiwar statement by the artist.

title: 悲傷成為共同承受的重量
Grief becomes a shared weight
body: 承托遺體的手與合掌祈禱的手
Hands that carry a body meet hands joined in prayer
caption:
努昂哀悼基督，約 1460–1465 年，胡桃木板繪畫
歸於讓・傅凱，努昂萊豐泰訥聖馬丁教堂，PM37000342

Pietà of Nouans, about 1460–1465, painting on walnut
Attributed to Jean Fouquet, Saint-Martin, Nouans-les-Fontaines, PM37000342
tw: 到了努昂這幅大型宗教畫，身體的重量變得格外直接。蒼白的基督橫向伸展，周圍的人用雙手承接遺體。聖母與捐獻者則合掌祈禱，讓承受重量的手和承受悲傷的手，出現在同一個場景。白色披巾、布料和肌膚彼此連結，密集的人群仍圍繞清楚中心。法國文化部以卸下十字架登錄這件作品，常用題名則是哀悼基督；兩種名稱讓我們注意受難敘事的不同時刻。作者也需要保留歸於傅凱的說法，定年仍有其他意見。右側捐獻者的確切身分，目前沒有定論。它今天仍保存在地方教堂，提醒我們傅凱作品的生命不限於首都博物館。從掌中小畫到公共宗教空間，穩定形體與清楚關係，始終讓觀看者找到進入故事的位置。
en: In this large religious painting at Nouans, bodily weight becomes immediate. Christ extends across the foreground while surrounding figures support him. The Virgin and the donor join their hands in prayer. Hands carrying a body and hands expressing grief occupy the same scene. White cloth and pale flesh connect the crowded group around a clear center. The French heritage register calls the subject a Descent from the Cross, while the familiar title is the Pietà of Nouans. Each directs attention to a different aspect of the Passion narrative. Attribution to Fouquet remains qualified, and alternative dates exist. The donor’s identity is also uncertain. The painting still belongs to a local church, reminding us that these works have lives beyond major museums. Across very different scales, stable bodies and clear relationships give viewers a place within the story.

title: 宏偉來自關係的清楚
Grandeur through clear relationships
body:
面孔讓身分可見
空間讓故事可以進入

Faces make identity visible
Space gives us a way into the story
caption:
艾蒂安・舍瓦利耶時禱書：聖母往見
讓・傅凱，1450 年代，羊皮紙彩飾，孔代博物館

Hours of Étienne Chevalier: The Visitation
Jean Fouquet, 1450s, illuminated parchment, Musée Condé
tw: 回顧這些作品，傅凱的宏偉感總與關係有關。國王以身體占據畫面，大臣以雙手連向畫外，祈禱書把個人帶進神聖歷史，宴會和會議則把權力安排成可以看懂的空間。今天，畫板、圓章與書頁散在不同地方，重新並看才讓部分關係回來。下次遇到一幅傅凱，除了留意鮮明色彩，也可以看看：人物朝向誰？目光走到哪裡？一個有限表面，又如何容納比它更大的世界？
en: Across these works, Fouquet’s grandeur grows from clear relationships. A king fills a frame. Joined hands reach beyond one. Prayer books connect individuals with sacred history, while tables and rooms give political order a visible form. Panels, medallions, and pages now survive in different places, so comparison helps recover some of their connections. The next time you meet a Fouquet image, follow its directions. Who turns toward whom? Where does your eye travel? How does a limited surface open onto a larger world?

tw: 感謝你和我們一起欣賞傅凱的藝術。歡迎再回來看畫，我們下次見！
en: Thank you for exploring Fouquet with us. We look forward to sharing more art with you. See you next time!
